title: How the Clarkson Art of Play treatment account was disputed
summary: Tracks Clarkson's quoted account of being treated as unable to afford a purchase and Owens's contrary interpretation of the same store encounter. These are competing attributed accounts, not an adjudication of discrimination.

milestones.label: Clarkson complaint quoted
milestones.proposition: In the post read by Owens, Clarkson says Art of Play treated her as unable to afford a purchase and compares the encounter to Pretty Woman.
milestones.review_note: Reviewed 2030–2168s and canonical quoted-post conveyance. Clarkson is the attributed author; Owens reads the post rather than Clarkson speaking live. The transcript alternates between tweet and Instagram, so the platform remains unspecified. This establishes a quoted complaint in this source, not an independently authenticated post or a discrimination finding; first_asserted means the entry account in this reviewed thread, not the earliest public allegation.
milestones.statement_text: Kelly Clarkson wrote that she drove to Art of Play in Brooklyn intending to buy things, felt she was viewed as unable to afford them, was offered something comparable, and compared the treatment to Julia Roberts' character in Pretty Woman, according to the post Owens read.

milestones.label: Owens disputes discrimination
milestones.proposition: Owens disputes Clarkson's treatment account, saying the displayed bird was not for sale and the employee offered another one rather than discriminating against her.
milestones.review_note: Reviewed 1942–2249s and statements-35129ca3971c / -7c852dbbba4e / -09b85c84aebd. This is Owens's contrary interpretation of the same encounter, including her commissioning-price explanation and reference to store video. The embedded Molly clip does not independently establish the encounter; neither discrimination nor its absence is adjudicated. The reported owner threats are a separate unverified aftermath claim and do not decide treatment or identify a threat actor.
milestones.statement_text: Owens said Kelly Clarkson was not discriminated against at Art of Play and that the employee simply said the displayed bird was not for sale and offered another one.
milestones.speaker: Candace Owens

links.review_note: Statement-7c852dbbba4e quotes Clarkson interpreting the store response as inability-to-afford treatment; statement-ac45ad9962fb expressly denies discrimination and characterizes it as an ordinary refusal to sell a display item. These are explicit competing accounts of the same encounter, not mere shared entities. The link records disagreement without deciding which is true; both milestones occur in this source as the skill permits.
